paragraphs: Friend, look at who is on that hill. The rulers sneer, the soldiers mock, and one of the criminals heaps abuse on Him, and all three tell Him to save Himself (Luke 23:35-39). Yet the first words we hear from the cross are "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." (Luke 23:34). That's the big idea, baker: Jesus doesn't get pushed into this, and He stays on that cross for the very people who are mocking Him.

Now look at the man hanging next to Him. He admits, "We are punished justly," and then he asks one thing: "Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!" (Luke 23:41-42). He has no good résumé, no time to fix anything and no cookies to bring, yet Jesus answers, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise." (Luke 23:43). So if you ever feel too far gone or too late, this man says come as you are, because you can't earn it and you don't have to.

Even as the sun goes dark, Jesus calls out, "Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit." (Luke 23:44-46). Right to the end He is talking to His Father and trusting Him with everything. Then a Roman centurion says of the One the rulers mocked, "Surely this was a righteous man." (Luke 23:47). So here's why my ovens stay ready, friend: you can trust the One who stayed on that cross, and this story is NOT done.
